sources.statement: of reminiscence therapy for dementia, with 1,972 people, were reviewed by Cochrane in 2018.
sources.label: Woods, O'Philbin, Farrell, Spector and Orrell, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2018, CD001120
sources.verified: Review summary page read 2026-10-28 via search result: 22 studies, 1,972 people. The size of any benefit was not confirmed, so none is claimed.

sources.statement: A 2015 study in Brain compared brain regions that hold long-term musical memory with Alzheimer's data and found they lose fewer neurons and show less metabolic decline than the rest of the brain.
sources.label: Jacobsen, Stelzer, Fritz, Chetelat, La Joie and Turner, Brain 138(8), 2438 to 2450, 2015
sources.verified: Citation and findings read 2026-10-28 from the Duke Scholars record and press coverage. Small sample; the paper's aim of therapeutic use is stated as a hope, not a result.

sources.statement: People tend to recall more personal memories from roughly ages 10 to 30, the reminiscence bump. A systematic review of 68 studies puts the span at about 10 to 30 years for important events and about 5 to 30 for word-cued memories.
sources.label: Munawar, Kuhn and Haque, Understanding the reminiscence bump: a systematic review, PLoS ONE, 2018
sources.verified: Findings read 2026-10-28 from the review's listing and abstract summary.

sources.statement: is a free leaflet that staff, family or carers fill in to record a person's background, important events, preferences and routines, so care can be tailored to the person.
